newsitem.title: USA: MSRB to ask dealers to report time of OS receipt.
newsitem.headline: MSRB to ask dealers to report time of OS receipt.

text.p: The MSRB said on Monday it will propose requiring bond dealers to furnish regulators information on when they receive official statements from issuer clients in primary offerings.

"The official statement is critically important for investors," Roger Hayes, chairman of the Municipal Securities Rulemaking Board, said in a news briefing. "The board is concerned with the timing of the preparation and dissemination of the official statement," he said.
Hayes said the board will propose an amendment to its rule G-36, which requires municipal bond dealers to file official statements with the board's electronic repository within certain timeframes.

Underwriters of primary offerings must file a copy with MSRB one day after getting the OS from the issuer and no later than 10 business days after a final agreement to purchase, offer or sell securities.
The National Association of Securities Dealers and Securities and Exchange Commission is reviewing whether some dealers have failed to comply with rule G-36 deadlines.
Dealers, however, warn that they are having legitimate problems in getting official statements from issuers on time to meet G-36 deadlines.

"(We will propose) changes to G-36 to get more information on the performance of issuers and underwriters," Hayes said. "We will collect information on when undewriters are getting the information from issuers."
He said the information will be supplied to the board, which will make the data available to the NASD and SEC.
Hayes also said the board will ask for comment from market participants on possible remedies for any breach of contract involving receipt of OSs.
He said the board will alert issuers and their agents that underwriters must get OSs in time to review the documents.

Hayes said the 15-member board also will request comment "on the practice of issuers selecting or influencing the selection of underwriter's counsel and whether there should be some sort of disclosure to investors in such instances."
